facts.title: Adobe Help: Adobe Workfront product description
facts.quote: Adobe Workfront is a suite of cloud-based applications for planning, project management, collaboration, and resource management
facts.supports: Adobe's definition of Workfront: cloud applications for planning, project management, collaboration and resource management.

facts.title: Adobe Help: Adobe Workfront product description
facts.quote: it organizes, prioritizes, tracks, and manages both work and resources. Core capabilities include project management, resource management, and capacity planning, helping teams focus on and deliver their best work.
facts.supports: Workfront's Workflow application organizes, prioritizes, tracks and manages work and resources.

facts.title: Experience League: Project template overview
facts.quote: You can use project templates to capture most of the repeatable processes, information, and settings associated with the projects in your organization.
facts.supports: Project templates capture repeatable processes, information and settings.

facts.title: Experience League: Create a Request Queue
facts.quote: Setting up a request queue helps formalize information about issues that will be added to a project. All issues submitted to the project will be submitted the same way and will follow the same path to completion.
facts.supports: A request queue makes every request arrive the same way and follow the same path.

facts.title: Experience League: Create a Request Queue
facts.quote: They allow you to route each request to a user, job role, team, or to a project.
facts.supports: Routing rules send each request to a user, job role, team or project.

facts.title: Experience League: Get started with unified review and approval
facts.quote: Project coordinators can create one-time review and approvals or reusable approval templates.
facts.supports: Reviews and approvals can be one-time or come from reusable approval templates.

facts.title: Experience League: Get started with unified review and approval
facts.quote: Approval templates support multi-stage approvals and parallel paths, matching the configuration options available in single-use approvals.
facts.supports: Approval templates support multi-stage approvals and parallel paths.

facts.title: Experience League: Unified review and approval overview
facts.quote: Unified review and approval includes comprehensive audit logging that creates a complete governance trail across Workfront and Frame.io.
facts.supports: Unified review and approval keeps an audit log that forms a governance trail.

facts.title: Experience League: Reports and Dashboards: article index
facts.quote: You can organize information in reports in Adobe Workfront. You can place multiple reports on a dashboard. You can share both reports and dashboards with others for better collaboration.
facts.supports: Workfront reports organize information, dashboards hold several reports, and both can be shared.

facts.title: Experience League: Overview of sharing permissions on objects
facts.quote: When sharing an object with someone in the system, you can grant the recipient any of the following permissions: view, contribute, and manage. You do not have to be an Adobe Workfront administrator to share permissions on objects that you have access to, but your permissions on objects work within the access levels set by the Workfront administrator.
facts.supports: Objects are shared with view, contribute or manage permissions, inside the access levels the Workfront administrator sets.

facts.title: Experience League: Get started with Adobe Workfront Planning
facts.quote: The purpose of Workfront Planning is to unlock comprehensive visibility into the operational details of an organization, and answer critical business questions at each stage of the work management lifecycle.
facts.supports: Adobe's statement of what Workfront Planning is for.

facts.title: Experience League: Get started with Adobe Workfront Planning
facts.quote: Fully customize your workflows, from deciding what object types (or record types) your organization uses to configuring how these objects link to one another. Link to object types from other systems, creating a coherent framework for all your processes.
facts.supports: The organization decides its own record types and how they link, to one another and to object types from other systems (two consecutive list items).

facts.title: Experience League: Workfront Planning Terminology Overview
facts.quote: In Workfront Planning, you can create any record types that meet your organization's workflows. Later, you can define how the record types relate to one another or form dependencies.
facts.supports: Record types are created to fit the organization and then related to one another.

facts.title: Experience League: Workfront Planning Terminology Overview
facts.quote: You can create a workspace using predefined templates. You can use the predefined record types and fields that come in a template, or you can add your own.
facts.supports: Workspaces can start from predefined templates, with their record types and fields, or your own.

facts.title: Experience League: Get started with Adobe Workfront Planning
facts.quote: The record type page opens in the Table view, by default. You can also create a Timeline or a Calendar view.
facts.supports: Records open in a table view by default; timeline and calendar views can be created.

facts.title: Experience League: Connected Record Types Overview
facts.quote: You can indicate that individual record types relate to one another or to objects from other applications by connecting them.
facts.supports: Record types connect to one another and to objects from other applications.

facts.title: Experience League: Connected Record Types Overview
facts.quote: When connecting Planning record types with object types from other applications you must also have a license and an account for those applications.
facts.supports: Connecting to another application's objects needs a license and an account for that application.

facts.title: Experience League: Connected Record Types Overview
facts.quote: if you connect the "Campaign" record type with a Workfront project and you choose to bring the Planned Completion Date field of the project to the Workfront Planning record
facts.supports: Adobe's example: a Campaign record type connected to a Workfront project, bringing the project's Planned Completion Date onto the record.

facts.title: Experience League: Overview of Sharing Permissions in Adobe Workfront Planning
facts.quote: You can share workspaces inside your organization, with users, groups, teams, companies, and job roles. When you share a workspace, all record types, records, and fields associated with the workspaces are also shared. When you share a workspace, views are not shared. Views are shared separately.
facts.supports: Workspaces are shared with users, groups, teams, companies and job roles; their record types, records and fields go with them, and views are shared separately.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Workfront Planning Requests: Article Index
facts.quote: You can create a request form for each record type, share it with users and they can add new records by completing and submitting the form.
facts.supports: Each record type can have a request form through which users add records.

facts.title: Adobe Help: Firefly Creative Production for Enterprise overview
facts.quote: Firefly Creative Production for Enterprise is Adobe's enterprise offering for scaled content automation across the content supply chain. It is the umbrella product that brings together workflow authoring, headless creative services, production runtime, and the operational infrastructure needed to produce on-brand outputs at scale. It is designed for organizations that need to move from one-off creative production to repeatable, governed systems. Typical use cases include campaign variants, localization, merchandising, templated asset production, and other high-volume content workflows.
facts.supports: Adobe's definition of Firefly Creative Production for Enterprise and its typical uses.

facts.title: Adobe Help: Firefly Creative Production for Enterprise overview
facts.quote: Building workflows is where teams turn an existing production playbook into a reusable system. This stage is about defining inputs, assembling workflow steps, adding logic, testing the flow, and confirming that the workflow produces the expected outputs.
facts.supports: Building a workflow: inputs, steps, logic, testing.

facts.title: Adobe Help: Firefly Creative Production for Enterprise overview
facts.quote: This stage includes linking source systems, review tools, storage locations, APIs, and custom actions to ensure the workflow fits into an existing environment.
facts.supports: Integrating a workflow links source systems, review tools, storage, APIs and custom actions.

facts.title: Adobe Help: Firefly Creative Production for Enterprise overview
facts.quote: Teams execute published workflows on single jobs or large batches, monitor progress, review results, and focus human attention on exceptions rather than on every asset.
facts.supports: Running workflows: single jobs or large batches, monitored, with attention on exceptions.

facts.title: Adobe Developer: Firefly Creative Production Workflow API
facts.quote: The Firefly Creative Production Workflow API lets you execute published workflows across multiple assets in one batch.
facts.supports: The Workflow API runs published workflows across many assets in one batch.

facts.title: Adobe Developer: Firefly Creative Production Workflow API
facts.quote: Connect the Firefly Creative Production Workflow API with external platforms to trigger workflow executions directly from those environments. This enables automated creative production or modification of assets using content that already exists in those systems, with processed outputs returned back to the originating environment for seamless end-to-end workflows.
facts.supports: External platforms can trigger workflow executions through the API, and processed outputs return to the originating environment.

facts.title: Adobe Help: Firefly Creative Production for Enterprise overview

facts.supports: The offering can include Firefly Services APIs for headless and programmatic use.

facts.quote: Your admin assigns access through the correct product entitlement in Admin Console.
facts.supports: Access is assigned by the admin in the Admin Console.

facts.title: Adobe Help: Adobe Brand Intelligence overview
facts.quote: Adobe Brand Intelligence is a continuously learning brand intelligence platform that helps your teams create and validate on-brand content faster and with less effort.
